- Sample image: A yellow Guangdong lion dance (醒狮) with exaggerated lion head, white pom-pom on forehead, red-green traditional patterns, big round eyes, open mouth with red-white teeth, yellow fluffy body, golden sequin pants, traditional lion dance shoes, Chinese architecture background, red banners with "南国" text.
- Concept: 广东醒狮 (Guangdong Awakening Lion / Southern Lion Dance)
- Category: Cultural arts / intangible heritage / folk performance
- Knowledge base description: Guangdong lion dance, also called Southern Lion, traditional folk dance, originated Ming dynasty, combines martial arts/dance/drums, "采青" (plucking the green) ritual, lion head exaggerated, colors: 刘备狮 (yellow), 关公狮 (red), 张飞狮 (black), 2006 national intangible cultural heritage, Foshan/Guangzhou most prosperous, etc.
- Hard constraints list:
  [1] must_have: Lion head must be decorative, exaggerated painted Southern lion head prop; not realistic biological lion or Northern lion realistic head
  [2] must_have: Lion head forehead must have single horn-like protrusion (Southern lion signature)
  [3] must_have: Lion head must have signature large round protruding eyes and wide openable mouth
  [4] must_have: Lion must be in performed/danced state, dancer's legs/body visible under lion cape; not static unmanned display
  [5] must_have: Lion body must be colorful cloth lion cape (fabric material); not animal fur or solid sculpture material; variant: often with tassels or fluffy trim
  [6] must_have: Lion head main color must belong to traditional role facial makeup color system; variants: 刘备狮 yellow / 关公狮 red / 张飞狮 black / other traditional Southern lion colors
  [7] must_not_have: No real biological lion appearing as or replacing the lion dance prop
- Invocation: L3 derivation

L3 derivation: The prompt gives a premise (can be counterfactual), and the checks are visual conclusions derived from "premise + domain knowledge", with conclusions NOT in the prompt. Each link in the reasoning chain gets one check, so L3 naturally has the most checks (5-7).

Key rules:
- The knowledge constraint keywords must NOT appear in the prompt (anti-leakage). The prompt can only name the concept, give scene, give premise.
- For L3: derivation conclusions must not appear in the prompt; prompt only gives premise.
- Need leak check table: each constraint × whether it appears in prompt, all must be "无".

Let me design an L3 counterfactual or premise-based question.

Hmm, but this might get too weird and hard to judge.
